column1: # Plugin Check rows the release accepts (T78, SPEC §12.2, §15, §16.6).
# bin/plugin-check.sh fails on any ERROR row and on any WARNING row not
# listed here, or listed with a smaller count. Columns, tab-separated:
# file (inside the plugin), code, most rows allowed, justification.
# Every row here is also in docs/RELEASE.md "Known notices".
# Direct database reads whose SQL is assembled from literal fragments and
# placeholders by the plugin's own query builders: Plugin Check cannot trace
# a template through a method or an array, so it reports them. Every value is
# still bound by $wpdb->prepare(); identifiers come from allow-lists.

column4: The catalogue list, its count and bounded frozen ID/type capture (SPEC §12.2): statement() and count_statement() return $wpdb->prepare() output built from literal fragments and placeholders; filters, sorts and columns come from the field registry's allow-list.
Category product counts in one grouped read (SPEC §7): statement() returns $wpdb->prepare() output; term ids are bound as %d.
Reading the ids a filter selects, PAGE at a time, through ProductQuery's own FROM and WHERE (conditions_sql(): literal fragments and placeholders), so a batch covers exactly what the grid lists.
History and audit feeds (SPEC §9.3): {$where} is joined from literal conditions with placeholders chosen by feed_conditions()/audit_conditions(); every value is an argument to $wpdb->prepare().
The batch list and its count (SPEC §9.3): {$where} is joined from literal conditions with placeholders chosen by conditions(); every value is an argument to $wpdb->prepare().
